cells.tense: A feeling is arriving now for the exact time it is arriving.
cells.ask: Say the sentence you have been holding about what you are feeling, to one person, before today closes. Do not plan what it will fix.
cells.core: Something is arriving and you can let it arrive. That sounds like nothing, and it is not nothing. People who push a direction forward often stop feeling it along the way; you have not — you can sit in the room with what someone just said and let it land before you decide what to do with it. What makes this balance fragile is that it looks like slowness. You have a direction. People expect the direction to keep moving, and feeling your way forward can read to them as hesitating. The receiving is what keeps the direction honest. Keep the position that lets the new thing in before it becomes a task or a threat, and accept that you will sometimes look slower than the room wants you to be. Notice what arrives before it hardens into a plan.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel the new thing before it becomes an item.
cells.verb: Letting what is actually here land before it hardens into a plan.
cells.place: A room where a direction is already moving and a head is deciding whether to speak.

cells.tense: The next complaint, the next praise, the next anything, is being felt before it has shown up.
cells.ask: Take one unassigned hour today and do something with your hands. When you catch yourself steering what is not yours to steer, put the hands back.
cells.core: You are bracing for a feeling that has not arrived, and it is costing you the ones that have. Someone opens their mouth and you have already decided what you will receive and how it will land. That is not openness, but it protects you from surprise. Your direction is fast. Racing ahead of a feeling means you arrive first and nobody meets you. The goal stops getting real information. Somewhere ahead a version of this exists where the goal is certain and no one can shake it, and you are living there instead of in the room you are in. Receiving is not a weaker sibling of driving. It is what tells you whether the direction is still yours. The room already holds what the next move needs, if you let it reach you.
cells.sheetLine: You feel the next verdict before anyone names it.

cells.tense: There was a moment, and the feeling stopped arriving after it.
cells.ask: Say one fresh sentence about what you want this week, out loud, where someone can hear it. The sentence is enough.
cells.core: You stopped feeling your way forward, and it had a logic at the time. Receiving something asked more of you than it gave, and the intelligent move was to stop. That move worked. The goal kept moving, the direction stayed clean, and nothing new lands on you unasked. What you lost is subtler. A direction that receives nothing goes nowhere except toward the finish. The old face of this is recognition that stays available, knowing that deepens instead of closing. The way back is to begin again in a small way. Say a thing before you know how it will land, and notice the gap between the guess and the fact.

cells.tense: The pen is already moving across a page that was never held out.
cells.ask: Ask one person one question you do not know the answer to. Sit through the reply and change nothing.
cells.core: You are already open, and you talk about it like a mood you are waiting on. Something lands and you have not received it. You chalk it up to circumstance, to the wrong day, to the other person's timing. The opening is yours. Do not make it a gift they brought. You may be the one choosing what gets through and then saying the situation had decided. Look at how you let things in, not at how smooth the conversation went. What you carry has a name that keeps changing. The face of this back in balance is knowing that keeps deepening instead of hardening. The plain move is to let the simple thing in and stop explaining how it got there.
cells.sheetLine: The opening is already yours, and you call it theirs.
